bið: bēon — is, will be (3rd singular present; the form Old English uses for general truths)
bād: bīdan — awaited, abode (3rd singular preterite; takes the genitive: the hall 'awaited' the fire)
cwæð: cweðan — said, declared (3rd singular preterite; cf. archaic 'quoth')
deniga: Dene — of the Danes (genitive plural, longer form; the prologue's Gār-Dena is the same people)
fela: fela — many, much (indeclinable; takes the genitive)
folcum: folc — among the folks, peoples (dative plural)
frēan: frēa — of the Lord (genitive singular of frēa 'lord'; here God)
fæst: fæst — fast, fixed, firm (adjective; wæs tō fæst on þām 'was too fixed in them')
fēond: fēond — fiend, enemy (nominative singular; literally 'the hating one' — present participle of fēogan 'to hate')
geardum: geard — in the courts, dwellings (dative plural; geard 'yard, enclosure' — cf. middangeard 'middle-earth')
gearwe: gearu — ready, prepared (adjective, nominative plural masculine) · gearwe — clearly, fully, well (adverb)
geatolīc: geatolīc — equipped, splendid, ready (adjective, accusative; from geatwe 'trappings')
gebād: gebīdan — experienced, lived to see (3rd singular preterite; takes the genitive)
guman: guma — men, warriors (nominative plural; the ancestor of '-groom' in 'bridegroom')
gēata: Gēatas — Geats, a people of what is now southern Sweden (genitive plural)
healfdenes: Healfdene — Healfdene, king of the Danes, father of Hrothgar (genitive)
higelāces: Higelāc — Higelac, king of the Geats (genitive)
him: hē — to him, or to them (dative singular or plural of hē)
hrōðgār: Hrōðgār — Hrothgar, king of the Danes, builder of Heorot (nominative)
hāten: hātan — called, named (past participle; wæs hāten 'was called')
hēold: healdan — held, ruled; kept (to a place) (3rd singular preterite) · healdan — kept, maintained (3rd singular preterite; with ǣgwearde: kept watch)
hūsa: hūs — of houses (genitive plural; hūsa sēlest 'best of houses' — Heorot's standing epithet)
hȳrdon: hȳran — obeyed (3rd plural preterite; takes the dative)
lēode: lēode — people, men (nominative plural) · lēode — people, men (accusative plural)
mid: mid — with (preposition; here after its object: him mid 'with him') · mid — with (preposition; also before its object: mid Gēatum 'with the Geats')
nacan: naca — of the ship, boat (genitive singular, weak masculine)
nihtum: niht — nights (dative plural; sweartum nihtum 'in the black nights')
nīð: nīð — malice, affliction, violent enmity (accusative singular)
ond: ond — and (the usual spelling of and in this MS)
oþ: oþ — until (with þæt: oþ þæt 'until'; variant spelling of oð)
rǣd: rǣd — counsel, plan, 'rede' (accusative singular; Æthelred 'the Unready' was un-rǣd — 'ill-counseled')
sceal: sculan — shall, must, ought by nature to (3rd singular present) · sculan — must, shall (1st singular present; ic sceal 'I must')
scolde: sculan — had to, was obliged to (3rd singular preterite)
scyldinga: Scyldingas — of the Scyldings, the descendants of Scyld = the Danes (genitive plural)
se: se — the, that (nominative singular masculine; unaccented spelling of sē)
sum: sum — one, a certain one; some (pronoun or adjective, often with a genitive: fīftȳna sum 'one of fifteen')
syþðan: siþþan — after, when (conjunction; another of its spellings)
sē: sē — he, that one; the (nominative singular masculine of the demonstrative; sē þe 'he who')
sēlest: sēlest — best (superlative; its comparative sēlla has no positive — 'good' is understood)
tō: tō — to, as, for (preposition) · tō — too (adverb; tō swȳð 'too severe') · tō — to (particle before the inflected infinitive: tō gecȳðanne 'for declaring')
weard: weard — guardian, watchman (nominative singular, masculine; cf. 'ward')
wintra: winter — of winters (genitive plural; years are counted in winters)
witan: witan — to know (infinitive; preterite-present verb, cf. 'wit')
witena: wita — of the counselors, wise men (genitive plural; the king's advisory council was the witan)
wið: wið — against; with (preposition; wið Gode 'against God')
wēl: wēl — well (adverb; wēl bið 'well be it')
æþele: æþele — noble, of high birth (adjective, nominative singular masculine)
ðæt: þæt — that (conjunction, here spelled ðæt; oð ðæt 'until')
þe: þe — who, which, that (the indeclinable relative particle)
þenden: þenden — while, as long as (conjunction; archaic)
þone: sē — whom, that (accusative singular masculine of the demonstrative, here relative)
þæs: þæt — for that, of that (genitive singular of the demonstrative: 'comfort for that')
þā: þā — then (adverb); also: those, the (plural demonstrative); who, which (relative) · when (conjunction)
ǣr: ǣr — before, previously (adverb; cf. archaic 'ere') · ǣr — before (conjunction; ǣr gē 'before you')
